sentences.text: The system treats passenger disruption information as a secondary planning signal that can refine, but not replace, capacity and safety constraints in traffic flow decisions.
Its purpose in this area is to help the Regional Flow Manager understand where a small metering adjustment may reduce downstream disruption without degrading the Airport Capacity Plan.
Airline Operations Coordinator sends the Passenger Misconnect Count.
The Airline Interface Adapter validates the timeliness, flight association, and airline ownership of connection-risk data before it is made available for operational use.
The Data Governance Steward defines the acceptable aggregation level so that the Regional Flow Platform does not expose passenger names, booking references, or protected itinerary details.

The Demand Prediction Service combines connection-risk indicators with aircraft readiness, scheduled bank structure, and forecast arrival variability to estimate the sensitivity of selected departures.
These estimates are advisory and do not create an entitlement for a flight to receive a favorable Calculated Takeoff Time.
The Slot Allocation Engine continues to apply the approved sequencing policy, runway capacity, airspace constraints, and published Ground Delay Program parameters as controlling inputs.
When several flights have similar operational priority, connection-risk information may be used as a tie breaker if the Business Rules Registry permits that use for the active operating state.
The Departure Metering Service can therefore recommend a minor hold, release, or resequencing action only when the change remains inside the available runway and surface movement envelope.
The Tower Supervisor retains authority over tactical runway sequencing and may reject any advisory that would impair safe separation, wake spacing, or local controller workload.
The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to determine whether a proposed metering adjustment can be supported by stand availability, pushback feasibility, and taxi route status.
The Airport Duty Manager uses the Airport CDM Portal to see whether airline recovery actions are concentrated in one bank or distributed across the operating day.

Typical airline recovery actions include flight retiming, aircraft substitution, passenger protection on later services, and selective holding of departures already inside normal operational tolerance.
The system records these actions as operational context rather than as passenger service tasks assigned to the airport flow management process.
The Regional Flow Manager may consider a recovery action credible only when it is aligned with a valid Target Off Block Time, crew availability status, and confirmed aircraft readiness.
If an airline indicates a recovery plan that depends on unrealistic turnaround timing, the Demand Prediction Service discounts the associated connection benefit.

During Adverse Weather Mode, passenger disruption indicators are normally given less influence because the Capacity Assessment Module and Sector Load Monitor have reduced flexibility to absorb discretionary changes.
During Recovery Phase, the same indicators can have greater practical value because metering margins may exist after the primary capacity constraint has begun to clear.
The Arrival Regulation Console may show inbound connection pressure as context for arrival rate discussions, but it does not convert passenger handling needs into a separate arrival priority scheme.
The Common Situation Display presents passenger disruption cues with clear labeling so that participants understand they are decision-support indicators, not commands.
Every accepted use of connection-risk information in a metering decision is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the responsible actor, rationale, and affected flight interval.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares later delay outcomes with the logged rationale to determine whether the advisory use of passenger disruption data improved recovery performance.

This approach keeps the primary system function focused on safe, efficient, and transparent traffic flow management while still allowing airline recovery information to inform proportionate metering choices.
